title: Youth for Democracy festival
body: Students' Councils from different countries visit a school's 'Youth for Democracy' festival. Team A: All students gather in one place and elect their president once a year, but the president has very limited powers. For major decisions, such as the canteen menu, they gather at a designated place and vote using ballot papers. Team B: The school holds elections every year. Every class elects a representative, who then takes part in electing the Students' Council President. The President and the representatives decide together. Team C: Students vote directly for the School President as well as for members of the Council. The President is both head of the Council and chief decision-maker. Team D: Elections are held, but only selected candidates are allowed to contest. The School President holds most of the power, the Council has very limited authority, and opposition voices are weak or discouraged.

title: Democracy at the grassroots: Jethipura Gram Panchayat
body: Jethipura Gram Panchayat in Block Idar, Sabarkantha district, Gujarat, received the Nanaji Deshmukh Rashtriya Gaurav Gram Sabha Puraskar in 2019 for its performance. It ensured that Gram Sabhas were held regularly and records were properly maintained, and it went further by organising Special Gram Sabhas. It acted on time on issues of education, sanitation and the welfare of women and children. It also held Mahila Sabhas and made sure Gram Sabhas had an adequate quorum, with active participation from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women.
